review:
I know we all hate super hand-holdy games but this goes so far in the opposite direction it's not even fun. There are many unintuitive mechanics/design choices that your only real option to understand how to play is to watch some videos on how to play. Incredibly lazy decisions made by the developer, I would not buy this game at regular price or even half price. It's also quite a hostile experience trying to play with a controller, so don't even bother. I'm sure it'll get better but everything feels so stiff and clunky - this is not a game that feels good to play, maybe it feels good to overcome... I'm getting a refund though and maybe I'll give it another go if it dips below $5.

I'm glad I caught myself before the 2 hour refund limit because some of the other reviews speak to issues that I wouldn't discover unless going much deeper into the game. If the controls weren't stiff and clunky, and they took 10 minutes to explain the basic mechanics of managing your raft (my first game I went to check out an island, my raft floated away, resources in the water despawned when my raft left, and I didn't have enough resources to build a new one, didn't know things could only be built on the raft, etc ,etc.)

It's also far to easy too die and far too punishing when you do, so the game itself doesn't even encourage learning how to play by playing. Maybe it's more fun if you have 4 people to gather resources, stab boars, and manage a single raft - but for me this was just 2 hours of my life wasted and filled with frustration.

It's not quite the full jank of atmospheres, but the comedic atmosphere and general whimsical nature of the game is to be enjoyed when exacerbated by someone laughing in your ear.

Very unique take on the survival game genre, but really overshadowed by tedious and boring game mechanics. We found the game to be more fun when abusing its glitches and bugs.

Everything I will be describing came from a multiplayer session with my friend. I don't have much experience regarding singleplayer.

The first few hours of raft are extremely tedious. Sometimes a run can end because the game decides, that no resources will drift your way when you badly need them. 

The normal loot collection loop is insanely tedious and boring. The shark non-stop being on your ass doesn't make it more fun. The game expects you to collect an absolutely ridiculous amount of wood, plastic and metal. Planting trees on your raft barely speeds it up and collecting them by hand nets barely anything to work with. Plastic only drifts into your raft and metal, scrap etc come from gathering next to islands. Don't even get me started on the processing times for some of the materials via the Smelter. Many of the games mechanics artificially inflate your game time for no real reason.

Weapon durability being low and no repair station make this even worse, since you have to always craft a completely fresh set of tools if they break.

Gathering animals is insanely tedious. We beat the entire story without finding a single llama, because they just didn't spawn. Meanwhile, we had like 6 chickens and a goat.

Equipment breaks really quick, to the point where it might not even be worth crafting. I expect the same with armor (we never crafted it). The bow has a learning curve behind it, but even after using it for 20 hours it still felt bad, especially against any flying enemy.

To circumvent the absolutely tedious general gameplay loop, we starting dupping items via an exploit with saving and loading a backup. Problem is, that even with the huge amounts of resources, we didn't have enough for what we wanted to do/basic tools + basic infrastructure. I have no idea how the game expects you to collect so much wood, plastic, metal, scrap and titanium, when some recipes already take a large amount of it and that's just to craft said thing once.

The game's story consists of random scattered notes and a few locations. It's just kinda there and not really super interesting. You could probably "beat" the game in less than 5 hours if you really tried. The story mostly serves to give you tools to survive better and move to the next story location. Some of the puzzles were fun / interesting, but a lot of the time it's very straightforward. Some where just "go here, find this, then come back". Those were not very fun.

There are definitely a lot of bugs in multiplayer at least. A big one we encountered was, that the advanced controls caused the advanced anchor to be in a superposition. It was lowered for me, but not for the other player, causing the raft to glitch out. Some other meaningful ones I can mention are: completely negating fall damage, climbing walls vertically etc.

Overall, the game expects you to put in a ridiculous amount of time gathering simple resources and doing the same thing over and over again (gathering treasure for example). Don't even get me started on the achievement list. It has to be one of the worst ones I've ever seen in a video game, nothing but do this x50 times for no real reason. No fun. The idea behind the game is good, but the execution of game mechanics really drags down the entire experience. I'm sure some people could enjoy a really slow paced survival game that takes real hours and that offers doing stuff over and over again. But I don't think tedious game mechanics and wasting your time for no reason is fun or engaging.

If you were looking for a raft-building survival crafting game that takes place on the water, this is the one to go to!

I think your alternatives are Tidewrack (not as well rated) or Stranded Deep (not raft-focused). It's fun, but there are some frustrations. Quite a number of tools are a mystery to unlock and use. In particular, I spent about 50 hours of the game just doing base building -- having fun, mind you -- before I realized I hadn't "researched" copper, which ludicrously unlocks circuit boards, then antennas, then radar and ... GPS mapping systems??? Until then you'll simply hit the same islands over and over and will never locate any of the storyline. And the storyline? Well it's fine. It's uneven. The story is about people who came before you, what happened to the world such that it's all so wet all over, and the struggles they dealt with. 

A lot of the tech tree is silly, just go in knowing that and you'll be fine. This is not ultrarealism. There is a meager list of nice-to-have items that make raft travel better but most are unlocked well into the story. For me I was already done at that point having put in nearly 100 hours. Some of that time was spent getting back up to speed: every time you die, you lose 2/3rds of your stuff. If you're playing multiplayer, apparently, you can be resuscitated by a friend, and keep your stuff, but if you're single player shame on you. There's no body you can fetch, you just lose most of your stuff, so make sure to leave unnecessary crap in a locker before you do a dangerous thing. 

Also quick tip don't do any renovating near your lockers or chests, because you may accidentally trigger a timespace conniption whereby all your contents try to exist in the same space at the same time and you lose almost everything. That was fun. I didn't throw anything across the room at all, I was very poised.

You use a  scrap hook to pick up scrap metal off the ocean floor, but the shovel won't work. You use a machete to strike a shark or warthog, but not an axe. You melt iron ore into metal bars which is used to build most heavy things, but you get nails from scrap which can't be likewise melted down. You can't use a shovel to row your raft, because that needs a paddle, and a paddle requires plastic. Lots of little things like that.

Still, you get to explore different islands, fight off sharks, build fairly big raft mobile homes if you want to invest the time, craft things into other things, and get an under-playtested but worthwhile back story. I had fun.

A brilliant, oceanic survival sandbox that transforms a stranded-at-sea nightmare into a deeply addictive and cozy crafting experience. You start on a tiny 2x2 wooden square armed only with a plastic hook, and your goal is to pull trash from the ocean to build a massive, floating fortress. The progression loop is incredibly rewarding as you transition from basic survival to automation and island exploration, though the repetitive early-game gathering and the relentless, annoying shark can test your patience.

PROS:
• Incredibly satisfying base-building that lets you build massive, fully customized rafts.
• Addictive progression loop from basic plastic-hooking to high-tech automation.
• Smooth and deeply engaging co-op experience—perfect to play with friends.
• Exploring unique, story-driven islands adds a refreshing break from drifting.

CONS:
• Early-game resource gathering can feel highly repetitive and slow.
• The shark mechanic is less scary and more of a constant, annoying chore.

[h1]游戏评测：《木筏求生 (Raft)》[/h1]
[h3]综合评分：8.5 / 10（蔚蓝汪洋中白手起家的漂流史诗）[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]画风与感官氛围 (8.8/10)[/b]：清爽的明快卡通视听，将海洋的孤独寂寥与碧海蓝天的度假感奇妙融合。
[*] [b]资源收集与循环 (8.5/10)[/b]：极具魔性的“勾垃圾”核心反馈，从单人前期手忙脚乱过渡到多人的快乐拆迁。
[*] [b]建筑自由与深度 (9.0/10)[/b]：强大的网格建造系统，支持玩家在漂流地基上生生手搓出一座移动的海上赛博堡垒。
[/list]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]中文评测[/h2]
在度过了无数个被鲨鱼咬碎地基、满海面拿钩子打捞塑料和木板的漂流夜晚后，我认为由 Redbeet Interactive 打造的《Raft》在百家争鸣的沙盒生存领域中，写下了一段独一无二的“空间限制”求生奇迹。它不同于传统生存游戏对无垠陆地的圈地征服，而是将玩家的命运死死绑定在了一座不断移动的生存母舰上。
[hr][/hr]
[h2]五大核心维度深度整合评测 (中文版)[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]1. 糖衣包裹的硬核危机（画面风格的奇妙反差）：[/b]
游戏的视觉采用了非常清爽、明快的卡通渲染风格。碧海蓝天、椰林树影，初看极具惬意的海岛度假感。但在这层无害的外表下，游戏塞满了各种极具压迫感的生存指标：高频消耗的饱食度与口渴值强迫你每天必须准时捕鱼、蒸馏海水，海鸥会偷吃作物，而海面下泛着寒光的鲨鱼则随时准备对你张开血盆大口。这种“画风越萌，死得越快”的反差感让生存前期充满了策略张度。
[*] [b]2. 从“黄金矿工”到自动化的魔性循环（核心收集机制）：[/b]
游戏最绝的设计，就是让玩家在一块 2x2 的木板上靠一把塑料钩子白手起家。扔出钩子、精准拖回飘来的塑料、木板、树叶和木桶，这种高度成瘾的交互逻辑极似3D版的“黄金矿工”。而随着科技树的解锁，当你终于能成排地铺满“自动收集网”，躺在躺椅上看着垃圾自己源源不断入库时，那种打破前期瓶颈、实现“垃圾收割自由”的爽感让人欲罢不能。
[*] [b]3. 违背地心引力的漂流奇迹（网格建筑深度）：[/b]
游戏基于网格坐标的建造系统赋予了极高维度的发挥空间。你的地基只是一座木筏，但你却可以通过立柱、楼梯和天花板，在公海上盖出一座几十层高的海上摩天大楼、航空母舰甚至是赛博朋克风的水上城堡。中后期加入的发动机、方向舵和锚固系统，更是能让你带着这座移动的“重工业奇迹”自由逆风航行，将“家”的移动城堡属性推向了极致。
[*] [b]4. 逼真的人工环境熵增压力（大白鲨 Bruce 的生态威慑）：[/b]
大白鲨（玩家戏称为 Bruce）是整款游戏关卡设计的神来之笔。它不仅会在你试图下海开采泥土、铁矿等核心资源时疯狂追杀你，更会定期浮出水面去啃咬、毁灭你的木筏地基。它是不可能被永久消灭的（杀死后几分钟内会重新刷新），这种永恒的、合理的自然威胁为游戏注入了高明的“熵增”压力，逼着你必须做出防御枪、不断用加固铁甲去强化每一块边缘地板。
[*] [b]5. 非线性“水下考古”叙事（剧情探索体验）：[/b]
与常规求生游戏的漫无目的不同，本作有着一条设计非常精妙的明线剧本。通过搭建雷达接收器与三根天线，在绿色的屏幕上定位一个又一个独特的剧情坐标。从荒废的海上高塔、被淹没的废土都市到盘踞着变异生物的科研海岛，每一个故事目的地都是完全独立的箱庭关卡。通过散落在各个角落的日记纸条、邮件，像侦探一样拼凑出人类世界被洪水淹没的后末日真相，剧情代入感极佳。
[/list]
[b]总结[/b]：总而言之，《木筏求生》用极低门槛的魔性操作，包裹住了一个宏大且极具纵深的海上重工业建造梦。无论你是想和好朋友来一场互相折磨、手忙脚乱的爆笑航海，还是渴望独自一人靠一把钩子撬动整座赛博海洋堡垒，它都是绝对不容错过的行业标杆级神作！
[hr][/hr]
[h2]English Review[/h2]
Raft by Redbeet Interactive is a triumphant, defining masterclass within the open-world survival genre, beautifully constructing an empire out of pure oceanic isolation. Shifting away from massive terrestrial landmasses, it forces players to tie their biological and creative survival entirely to an evolving, customizable floating home. Armed with nothing but a basic plastic hook to dredge drifting debris, you slowly climb a steep, industrializing tech tree while constantly warding off a relentless, ever-present shark threat. It masterfully fuses a bright, colorful cartoon aesthetic with intense mechanical stakes and non-linear, post-apocalyptic narrative ruins. It is an incredible, immensely addictive journey that treats the classic "zero-to-hero" crafting loop with absolute mechanical respect.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]5 Core Dimensions Integrated Review (English Version)[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]1. Hardcore Crises in Candy Wrapping (Visual Style Contrast):[/b]
The visual presentation utilizes a clean, vibrant cartoon-rendered aesthetic. The azure sky and tropical island silhouettes initially evoke a relaxing resort holiday vibes. However, beneath this harmless veneer lies an oppressive array of survival metrics: rapidly depleting hunger and thirst bars force you to fish and distill water constantly, seagulls pillage your crops, and a razor-fanged shark relentlessly patrols the perimeter. This sharp contrast between a cute art style and deadly stakes creates immense tactical tension early on.
[*] [b]2. From "Gold Miner" to Mechanical Automation (Core Collection Loop):[/b]
The game’s absolute hook is forcing players to survive on a tiny 2x2 wooden grid armed with nothing but a plastic hook. Throwing the hook and pulling in drifting plastic, wood, leaves, and barrels creates a deeply addictive mechanical loop. As the tech tree advances, placing a grid of "collection nets" allows you to lounge around while junk automatically streams into your inventory, transforming an exhausting grind into a satisfying harvest.
[*] [b]3. Architectural Miracles Defying Gravity (Grid-Based Construction):[/b]
The coordinate-based grid system unlocks boundless spatial freedom. Though your foundation is a mere raft, you can leverage pillars, stairs, and ceilings to construct multi-story skyscrapers, aircraft carriers, or cyberpunk-inspired floating fortresses on the high seas. The inclusion of late-game engines, steering wheels, and anchor systems turns this mobile industrial anomaly into a true wanderer, pushing the concept of a "home on the move" to its absolute peak.
[*] [b]4. Organic Environmental Stress (The Ecological Threat of Bruce):[/b]
The great white shark (lovingly dubbed "Bruce" by the community) is a structural masterstroke in level design. It doesn't just hunt you down when diving for rare iron or clay; it periodically surfaces to violently tear chunks out of your raft's foundation. It cannot be permanently eradicated, as a new threat spawns shortly after its death. This persistent environmental hazard injects an ingenious layer of stress, forcing you to craft metal armor plates and reinforce your home's borders.
[*] [b]5. Non-Linear Oceanic Archaeology (Story Exploration & Lore):[/b]
Departing from standard, aimless sandboxes, Raft features a beautifully paced linear narrative thread. By crafting a radar receiver and three antennas, you track glowing coordinate pings across a vast green display. From abandoned high-rise marine towers and submerged dystopian megacities to heavily guarded research eco-domes, each destination is an independent sandbox level. Piece-by-piece, players scour diaries and old emails to solve the post-apocalyptic riddle of a drowned world.
[b]Conclusion[/b]: Overall, Raft transcends the typical survival sandbox to deliver a profoundly structured, tactical experience built entirely on spatial adaptation. With its highly addictive core harvesting loop, intricate engineering progression, and beautifully layered box-set narrative encounters, it offers unparalleled late-night replayability. It stands as a flawless monument of creative survival that completely honors its mechanics and player agency.
[/list]

路人：大佬，带我一个呗！
阿强：不行，我要带上我家旺财！
阿强：三分钟一局，巨爽巨解压！疯狂水世界启动！
游戏总体对得起这个价格，但是联机体验奇差无比，错误非常多优化差，连接出错都是家常便饭，根据网上教程解决完可能昨天玩还正常第二天又开始出一样的问题，很搞心态，想联机来直接走吧，单人就随意了
这游戏我给了很多机会，联机一直很垃圾，跟朋友玩一直进不去显示联机出错。我已经找过办法了，以为是自己设备的问题，实际玩下来就是这破游戏的问题，浪费金钱浪费时间浪费精力。别跟我说联机不了就一个人玩，我说白了一个人玩这个有什么意思。
是我玩过最好玩的游戏！

疯狂水世界，启动！
适合几（2-8）个朋友一起玩的休闲生存游戏。当然单人也能玩。100+小时游戏时长，还是很有诚意的。几年前玩过一次，现在完整版更多内容，更多乐趣。
只有玩了才知道多好玩
终于圆梦了，小时候看小浪玩馋死我了
捡不完的垃圾，特别上头，想休闲一点的可以造船搭建，想忙一点的可以做主线任务，怎么开心怎么来，一个人也能玩得很开心!
超级典型的那种一个人玩很容易腻，但是人一多和朋友一起就贼欢乐的游戏，20出头的游戏流程不算长，但是一起玩的时候还是很欢乐的
